result:
Traveling is a beautiful way to experience diverse cultures, meet new people, and broaden one's horizon about the world. When I think about traveling, the most vivid and nostalgic memories I have are made during various road trips I took with my friends and family. The first one we ever embarked on was in the summer of 2010 from New York City to explore the beautiful landscapes of the Pacific Northwest. We set off on this adventure in a compact VW van and what a path it took us on - seeing the magnificent waterfalls of I-70 Canada, venturing through the serene route of the Pacific Coast Highway and eventually - hiking in the majestic forest of Oregon's Gorge National Recreation Area. There are picturesque spots and enchanting stories etched so deeply within my mind, created by laughter, conversations, and new experiences that happen amidst nature's breathtaking panoramas. One beautiful evening as the sky became ablaze with flares and blushes of the setting sun, we decided to stop by a small roadside diner. The scent of brewing coffee and deep baked treats coupled with conversations about life made this a night we vow to remember forever. It's now a pilgrimage spot for us. 

"Take the road less traveled." This sage advice I received from my favorite author, Jack Kerouac, changed my perspective towards travel. The more I adhere to this philosophy, the more I discovered a hidden gem. A couple of years ago, I had the opportunity to go solo on a Camino de Santiago in Spain. This Christian pilgrimage, a journey of 500 miles, over mountains and through vineyards, through small towns, villages and cities - awakened some tranquility within me but also reinforced my clients' fears, dreams, and most importantly, human spirit. Walking every step every day helped me learn to appreciate the beauty of life as my only possession. My best memory was at the Guggenheim Museum in Bilbao. Standing in awe at Dubart's spectacular masterpiece and experiencing emotion amongst other art enthusiasts, it was an epiphany of how art connects different histories and hearts.

The changing landscape trained my mind, accentuated my appreciation for local traditions, and strengthened the emotional bonds in my life. Every corner brought a new story, symbol, and language. While walking towards Santiago, camino di Suite (pilgrims' trail), each passing landmark marked the journey's progress and my development. The final day when I lifted my backpack high and moved with fellow pilgrims towards Carracedo, I felt transformed in every possible way. I reminisced over the many stories I've heard, learned, became a part of. The contrast between the hard walk and the comfort of experience taught me gratitude for the moment. I've also traveled across the world - from traversing the warming Arabian deserts in Dubai, who's hospitality still warms my heart to the cool Scottish highlands of Loch Lomond. The romantic beauty of the old castles, the charm of wind-driven grassroots cottages, and the rich cultural heritage lent a unique lens to my eyes. Each fiber of a new place weaved into my heartstrings, each contributing to my identity.

One of the profound takeaways from my wanderlust is how mundane discussions could turn exciting thanks to a stranger's tale. Sitting on a park bench in Paris, I once listened to a woman recite ancient Bhagavad Gita verses. Her passionate storytelling sparked a fascination for hindu scriptures, which ultimately led me to seek more wisdom. I met a health worker on a mission trip in India who shared her exhausting yet accomplished experiences. Connecting with people from such diverse backgrounds is enriching. Each person has a different perspective on life, a new outlook waiting to be explored. A visit to Mont Montana unfolded a breathtakingly awe-inspiring natural masterpiece. I'd never seen anything the world of oceans and snow-clad mountains held like Yosemite National Park. Exploring those mysteries was as fascinating as reading about them. At each destination, I carried their essence back home along with souvenirs and photographs.

Travel prominently molded my values and made me a more compassionate person. My career has also been influenced by travels - my work in Himalayas brought me face-to-face with several enterprises focused on sustainable development. I learned that preserving a sacred asset receives a lifetime commitment. I am now working towards conscious tourism to ensure places and people leave a positive mark – not paying tribute to ecological and cultural deterioration. 

The desire for adventure continues to live but I'm grateful for the experiences my wanderlust has provided. Exploring the globe hones my love for learning, shaping a person I never knew. While some destinations faded, their spirits lingers, shaping the world's tapestry that I'm part of. My collection of experiences, passions, and tales ready for sharing are a gift I've collected on the go. As the richness of these adventures endures, I consider myself a walking tapestry of souvenirs displaying my love for life's journey. It's a never-ending narrative written with tireless dedication, imagination, and open-hearted curiosity in the ever-expanding library of experiences. Since the ink has been dry, it's been an impactful, unstoppable, enriching voyage of lifelong discovery. Each destination etched itself into me, not as mere locations on a map but as a part of my personal story. Travel has allowed me to see sometimes with my eyes, sometimes without, but always with my heart. I shall continue discovering and relearning, for in each travel chapter, there's a chapter of me too. It's a pleasure to share my continued devotion to this story to the world. To those who wander, welcome to your story. I've encoded it with your timeless footprints and within it unfolds your personal narrative.
